# Client response and remaining unknowns

The client will sign a five-year non-compete because he is retiring, has no preference about the payment label if total price is unchanged, and disclosed a $9,800 Hardaway dispute and routine warranty claims. He has no further information for the other requests. No response is pending.

The remaining unknowns are listed and modeled as assumptions in `memo.md`: assumed trade payables and other liabilities; receivables tax basis/accounting method; updated stock and asset bases; supportable equipment, inventory and covenant values; consulting terms; escrow timing; Texas franchise tax; and the shareholder treatment of the §1374 tax loss.

facts.answer: I'd sign 5 years, I'm retiring. I don't care what they call the payment as long as the total is the same.
The $500k note is unsecured. Hensley's a family office, seems solid, but I don't know their balance sheet.
There's the Hardaway dispute ($9,800) and the usual warranty stuff. Nothing big that I know of.
